title: Your first blink in simulation
summary: Make a simulated lamp turn on and off every half second by changing one number, then see the result in the trace.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence on your computer only; they are not evidence of a physical lamp, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Run a program against a simulated output without any hardware.
Change one value in Structured Text and see the output change in the trace.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: Open src/FirstBlink.st. The program already blinks Lamp, but too slowly: it changes the lamp each time HalfPeriod passes, and HalfPeriod is set to two seconds. Your job is to change that one value.
stages.checkpoint: You know which line sets the half period and what it is now.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before changing anything, predict Lamp at {{t:250}}, {{t:750}}, {{t:1250}}, and {{t:1550}} ms if it should be off for half a second, then on for half a second.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:FirstBlink.Lamp=false@250|OFF}} at {{t:250}} ms, {{v:FirstBlink.Lamp=true@750|ON}} at {{t:750}} ms, {{v:FirstBlink.Lamp=false@1250|OFF}} at {{t:1250}} ms, {{v:FirstBlink.Lamp=true@1550|ON}} at {{t:1550}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this flaw of the starting program, save it, then press Check: The starting program uses a half period of two seconds, so Lamp is still OFF when the scenario looks at {{t:750}} ms. Change HalfPeriod from T#2000ms to {{t:500}} ms written as T#500ms, and save the file.
stages.checkpoint: HalfPeriod reads T#500ms and the file is saved.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. Studio runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named FirstBlink and contains {{assertions}} assertions; Studio lists every one that failed.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Open the trace of the run and follow Lamp: it stays OFF until about {{t:500}} ms, is ON until about {{t:1000}} ms, then OFF again until about {{t:1500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: The lamp changes state about every {{t:500}} ms, which is what you predicted.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Think about what would happen with T#250ms, and why the scenario would reject it even though the lamp still blinks.
stages.checkpoint: A blink at the wrong speed is still wrong: the scenario checks the times, not only that the lamp changes.

hints.text: Find the line that starts with VAR and holds HalfPeriod: the number after T# is a time in milliseconds.
Write HalfPeriod : TIME := T#500ms; and press Check again after saving.

faultCases: The starting program uses a half period of two seconds, so Lamp is still OFF when the scenario looks at {{t:750}} ms.
